core.title: Keep artifact-name hierarchy and variant depth shallow
core.given: The planner is choosing or reconsidering an artifact name
core.when: Deciding how many hierarchy levels and variant levels the name has
core.then: Keep hierarchy at 2-3 levels (4-5 max, sparingly) and variants at 0-1 variant levels (2 max), with each separator adding clear semantic value.
prefer: Remove a separator (and its level) when it does not add clear semantic value
avoid: Hierarchy beyond 5 levels; using 4-5 levels routinely rather than sparingly
More than 2 variant levels; multiple variant levels often indicate over-specification
Any separator that does not add clear semantic value, at any depth
core.why: Depth is the recommended nesting per separator; multiple variant levels often indicate over-specification, so each separator must add clear semantic value.
evidence: Each artifact name considered has at most 5 hierarchy levels and at most 2 variant levels
4-5 hierarchy levels are used sparingly, not as the norm
For every separator in the name, its semantic value can be stated
verification: Term 'depth' = the recommended nesting depth per separator
Thresholds: hierarchy_typical=2-3 levels; hierarchy_maximum=4-5 levels (use sparingly); variant_typical=0-1 levels; variant_maximum=2 levels
Warning: multiple variant levels often indicate over-specification
Level counting is mechanical: hierarchy levels are counted using the hierarchy separator and variant levels using the variant separator, both supplied by the profile's naming scheme
The check must inspect every artifact name considered, at any depth, not only new or deeper ones
Whether each separator adds clear semantic value cannot be counted mechanically; it is judged, and applies at any depth

values: artifact name exceeds the depth thresholds
a separator adds no clear semantic value
a separator adds no clear semantic value

fires: The planner names an artifact using 4-5 hierarchy levels where fewer would carry the same meaning
The planner names an artifact with more than 5 hierarchy levels
The planner names an artifact with 2 or more variant levels, or more than 2
The planner names an artifact at typical depth (2-3 hierarchy levels, 0-1 variant levels) but one separator adds no clear semantic value
The planner renames an artifact without changing its depth, and the resulting name contains a separator with no clear semantic value
The planner reviews or keeps an existing artifact name whose depth or separators are being considered
doesNotFire: The work does not involve choosing, reviewing or changing any artifact name
Deciding which separator character expresses which relationship (the separate separator-semantics convention), as opposed to how deep each goes

neutralityNotes: The rule is almost entirely stack-neutral (thresholds, sparingly qualifier, any-depth scope including same-depth renames, llm_judged semantic value). The only concrete content is the two separators: the variant separator (the dot) and the hierarchy separator, which the Bun realization delegates to its sibling separator-semantics convention. Both are naming-scheme data, so the core takes them from the profile via two proposed keys (urn.grammar#variant_separator, urn.grammar#hierarchy_separator); until the owner approves them, instantiating this core for another stack requires stating both separator characters. Finding ids (artifact_name_depth_exceeded, separator_without_semantic_value) stay bunOnly per the notProfileKeys list; the core describes the findings and the check generically. Activation-fact notes were non-obligating prose; their verifier-relevant content (inspect every name considered at any depth; semantic value judged at any depth) moved into core verification. The Bun 'unless' array is empty and the core adds no exceptions.
